title: 1999 HMMT February Oral Problem 3
statement: If \(x, y\), and \(z\) are distinct positive integers such that \(x^{2}+y^{2}=z^{3}\), what is the smallest possible value of \(x+y+z\).

solutions.text:
If \(z>5\), then \(z \geq 6\), so \(z^{3} \geq 216\). Now \(x^{2}+y^{2} \geq 216\), so \(x \geq 11\) and \(y \geq 1\), thus \(x+y+z \geq 18\). Since \(x=11, y=1, z=6\) does not work, we must have \(x+y+z>18\), and the solution given is the best possible.

Score 20 points for the correct answer, 5 points for justifying that we can't do better with \(z \leq 5,5\) points for justifying that we can't do better with \(z>5\).
